hook_text: Gold is Au. Iron is Fe. Lead is Pb. Who came up with these weird symbols?
clip_script: Every element on the Periodic Table has a short name, a symbol. Most make sense: H for hydrogen, O for oxygen, C for carbon. But some look wrong. Gold is Au, from the Latin aurum. Iron is Fe, from ferrum. Sodium is Na, from natrium. And lead is Pb, from plumbum, which is why fixing pipes is called plumbing. Latin was the shared language of science, so a chemist anywhere on Earth reads these the same way. Rule: first letter capital, second letter small. Now the ID number. Each element's atomic number is how many protons are in its atoms. Gold has seventy-nine. Lead has eighty-two. Change the protons, change the element, which is why no chemist could ever turn lead into gold.
visual_style: Whiteboard element squares for Au, Fe, Na and Pb with Latin words sliding out of them; a plumber's pipe; a nucleus counting up to 79 protons.
mood: Fun trivia with a big idea.
pacing: Quick symbol puzzles, a short rule, a satisfying alchemy twist.
